summary.description: A colourless, highly volatile liquid with a distinctive smell, classified as a volatile organic compound (VOC).
emission_sources: Use as a chemical intermediate in pesticide production
environmental_impact: High exposure can damage skin, liver, kidneys, and nervous system
Reacts in the air with other pollutants to form harmful ground-level ozone
Persists in water bodies but does not bioaccumulate in soils or sediments

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: High levels of chloroform exposure can harm multiple organs and contribute to harmful ozone formation, which negatively affects respiratory health.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Chloroform emissions primarily result from industrial and chemical use, emphasizing the need for improved handling and sustainable production practices.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG11_Sustainable_Cities_and_Communities: As a VOC contributing to urban air pollution and ground-level ozone, chloroform affects air quality in cities and the health of urban populations.
